name: Apple
selection: Pick one that feels heavy for its size with taut, unbroken skin. Press gently near the shoulder — it should not give at all. Dull skin and a slightly shriveled stem end mean long storage.
storage: Refrigerate. Apples last months cold and go mealy within a week on the counter.

varieties.name: Gala
varieties.note: Mild and sweet, thin skin. The first good apple of the season.

varieties.name: Honeycrisp
varieties.note: Coarse, shattering texture. Best eaten within weeks of harvest.

varieties.name: Red Delicious
varieties.note: Thick skin, soft flesh. Fades faster in storage than most.

varieties.name: Granny Smith
varieties.note: Hard and tart. Holds its texture in storage better than any other common variety.

varieties.name: Fuji
varieties.note: Dense and very sweet. Stores well.

varieties.name: Pink Lady
varieties.note: Late harvest, tart and firm. The last fresh apple of the year.
